SR-001.justification: Denied read, create and exec outside the policy each give a literal rule on that path with that access; applied, the respawn performs it while the sibling file stays denied, and the diff shows only the rule and the base's metadata reads on its way; a_denied_socket_connect_suggests_the_socket gives the socket path; the unit table in crates/procage/src/suggest.rs covers every file operation prefix.

SR-002.justification: A denial of the secrets class (listing ~/Library/Keychains) yields none on the kernel; spawn_linux.rs::a_refused_call_suggests_its_class_waiver shows none for setsid under Lifetime::Run and a refused socket family; the unit test nothing_without_a_safe_change covers the raw layer, the older-kernel guard, the proxy and unknown kinds.

SR-003.justification: A protect rule and a hide rule give their removal and a trust-handoff denial its waiver, each with weakens() true, and the respawn performs the operation; the Linux ptrace denial gives the process-access waiver marked weakening; grants and sockets are not marked (unit test only_grants_do_not_weaken).

SR-004.justification: Every case spawns again with the old policy after apply and asserts the operation is still denied; apply takes the policy by reference and returns a new one (crates/procage-policy/src/suggest.rs), and no API takes a running child.

SR-005.justification: explain::diff of old and new only loosens and names only the suggested rule (with its base metadata reads or rename anchors) or the waived class; the respawned run's receipt lists the trust-handoff waiver; the unit test apply_changes_exactly_one_thing compares each applied policy with the hand-made expected one.
